answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks the way a coral reef resists erosion: every identity must anchor a refundable stake, like a marble dropped into the ocean — cheap to place once, ruinous to place a thousand times. A new agent locks a bond for 100 epochs; peers attest its work, and any agent caught duplicating identities loses its stake to slashing. Honest agents earn the bond back with interest, while an attacker spawning ten thousand fakes must fund ten thousand bonds but still cannot fake peer attestations without doing work. The cost scales with the attack, but the reward does not.
